scope.dataset: ABIDE-derived processed cohort used by Experiment 53.3
scope.atlas_transfer: The cited 2026 normative ASD studies used different parcellations and cohorts. No cited regional/network result is assigned to a specific current feature.

ASD.medical_description: In autism, atypical functional connectivity can vary substantially from one person to another at the individual-connection level.
ASD.source_paper: Ilioska et al. Multiscale heterogeneity of atypical functional connectivity in autism. Nature Mental Health (2026).
ASD.evidence_scope: Normative modeling in a separate multisite cohort of 796 autistic and 1028 neurotypical participants; cross-sectional population result.
ASD.confidence_and_limitation: The study reports no single FC estimate with extreme normative deviation in more than 4% of either group. This is not a per-person diagnostic rule.
ASD.observable_evidence: The model has 256 current FC values, but no source-study normative z scores, individual subtype labels, or matching atlas-level regional map.

ASD.medical_description: Connection-level variability in autism can coexist with convergence of atypical connectivity across regions and larger functional networks.
ASD.source_paper: Ilioska et al. Multiscale heterogeneity of atypical functional connectivity in autism. Nature Mental Health (2026).
ASD.evidence_scope: Regional and network-level convergence in the cited cohort; not an annotation of this experiment's selected edges.
ASD.direction: heterogeneous at connection level; convergence at broader scales
ASD.confidence_and_limitation: The cited analysis used Schaefer cortical parcels and subcortical regions; exact regional labels are not transferred to the current Harvard-Oxford feature map.
ASD.observable_evidence: Requires regional aggregation and atlas correspondence not present in the 256-value model input.

ASD.medical_description: Autism cohorts can contain both lower-connectivity and higher-connectivity patterns, so a single direction should not be imposed on every person.
ASD.source_paper: Ilioska et al. Multiscale heterogeneity of atypical functional connectivity in autism. Nature Mental Health (2026); autism subtype analyses in Nature Neuroscience (2026).
ASD.evidence_scope: Separate large multisite cohorts; the subtype analysis found replicable hypo- and hyperconnectivity-dominant subgroups accounting for a minority of autistic participants.
ASD.direction: both positive and negative deviations occur across people
ASD.confidence_and_limitation: Subgroup-level evidence does not identify the subtype of any Experiment 60 participant.
ASD.observable_evidence: No normative deviation estimates or independently validated subgroup assignments are available.

ASD.medical_description: Some autistic participants show convergent lower functional connectivity in sensorimotor and attention-associated regions.
ASD.source_paper: Ilioska et al. Multiscale heterogeneity of atypical functional connectivity in autism. Nature Mental Health (2026).
ASD.evidence_scope: Group-level convergence in the cited multisite cohort, alongside pronounced individual-edge heterogeneity.
ASD.direction: lower connectivity at an aggregate level in some regions
ASD.confidence_and_limitation: No exact current ROI/edge or individual expected direction is established; this is not a universal ASD profile.
ASD.observable_evidence: Current FC values exist, but the required region/network grouping and person-specific normative reference are unavailable.

ASD.medical_description: The cited autism cohort showed convergent higher connectivity between frontoparietal and default-mode networks at an aggregate network scale.
ASD.source_paper: Ilioska et al. Multiscale heterogeneity of atypical functional connectivity in autism. Nature Mental Health (2026).
ASD.evidence_scope: Network-pair result from a cohort and parcellation different from Experiment 60.
ASD.direction: higher between-network connectivity in the cited aggregate analysis
ASD.confidence_and_limitation: Experiment 11's recovered ROI names do not provide a validated mapping to the cited network definitions; no edge-level claim is made.
ASD.observable_evidence: The model lacks the cited network assignments and normative residuals.

ASD.medical_description: Large multisite analyses have reported reproducible autism subgroups with predominantly lower or higher functional connectivity and different network patterns.
ASD.source_paper: Autism subtypes identified using cross-species functional connectivity analyses. Nature Neuroscience (2026).
ASD.evidence_scope: Cross-species analysis with independent human discovery/replication samples; the identified subtypes covered about one quarter of the examined autistic cohort.
ASD.direction: one subgroup predominantly lower; another predominantly higher
ASD.confidence_and_limitation: Subtype membership is not supplied for the Experiment 60 cohort; the findings do not establish an individual causal or biological subtype.
ASD.observable_evidence: The current classifier input has no external subtype labels or matching subtype-generation pipeline.

TD.medical_description: In typical healthy adults, resting-state fMRI reveals reproducible patterns of correlated activity among functionally connected brain regions.
TD.source_paper: Damoiseaux et al. Consistent resting-state networks across healthy subjects. PNAS (2006).
TD.evidence_scope: Resting-state network organization in healthy participants; a population-level reference rather than an individual diagnostic template.
TD.direction: within-network positive association at an aggregate functional-network level
TD.confidence_and_limitation: The cited networks are not mapped edge-for-edge onto the current 256 features.
TD.observable_evidence: Current values are pairwise FC, but current network assignments are not verified.

TD.medical_description: Resting-state functional organization can include anticorrelation between distributed networks as well as correlation within networks.
TD.source_paper: Fox et al. The human brain is intrinsically organized into dynamic, anticorrelated functional networks. PNAS (2005).
TD.evidence_scope: General resting-state organization in healthy adults; not an ASD-versus-TD edge rule.
TD.direction: negative association between some network-level signals
TD.confidence_and_limitation: A network-level result cannot be applied to a named Experiment 60 edge without independent mapping.
TD.observable_evidence: The current model does not use the cited network time series or validated network membership.

TD.medical_description: Several resting-state network patterns can be detected consistently across healthy participants.
TD.source_paper: Damoiseaux et al. Consistent resting-state networks across healthy subjects. PNAS (2006).
TD.evidence_scope: Group reproducibility across healthy subjects under the source study's acquisition and analysis conditions.
TD.direction: recurrent network organization, with individual variation
TD.confidence_and_limitation: It does not imply identical FC values or a disease-free feature vector for every control.
TD.observable_evidence: A single subject's current 256 values do not estimate cross-subject network reproducibility.

TD.medical_description: Functional connectivity reference distributions may depend on age, sex and head-motion characteristics, which should be accounted for in normative comparisons.
TD.source_paper: Ilioska et al. Multiscale heterogeneity of atypical functional connectivity in autism. Nature Mental Health (2026).
TD.evidence_scope: The cited cohort modeled connection values using age, sex and mean framewise displacement; this is a method description, not evidence that all covariates are available here.
TD.confidence_and_limitation: Experiment 60 has categorical age bins, sex and site, but does not establish the cited normative model or include the same motion variable in the DSS input.
TD.observable_evidence: The classifier receives raw processed FC and categorical PHENO; it has no fitted normative residuals.

TD.medical_description: In the cited healthy comparison group, extreme normative deviation at any one functional connection was uncommon at the individual level.
TD.source_paper: Ilioska et al. Multiscale heterogeneity of atypical functional connectivity in autism. Nature Mental Health (2026).
TD.evidence_scope: Study-specific threshold and cohort; no single FC estimate showed extreme deviation in more than 4% of either group.
TD.confidence_and_limitation: The 4% result must not be imported as a threshold for Experiment 60 or as a subject-level expected probability.
TD.observable_evidence: No Experiment 60 normative distribution or extreme-deviation labels are constructed.

TD.medical_description: A typical-control connectivity distribution is a comparison reference; deviation from it alone is not a diagnosis of autism.
TD.source_paper: Ilioska et al. Multiscale heterogeneity of atypical functional connectivity in autism. Nature Mental Health (2026).
TD.evidence_scope: Interpretive boundary implied by the cohort's normative analyses and explicit absence of validated person-specific biomarkers.
TD.confidence_and_limitation: This statement constrains interpretation and is not itself a discriminative biological marker.
TD.observable_evidence: It is a limitation statement, not a measured input feature.
